quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. Use your left foot to operate it. Lift your foot under the lever to shift up to a higher gear. Press the lever down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: Which item should you NOT check during a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluids, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: What kind of penalties does Oregon impose for drinking and riding?

options.text: Up to a judge to decide.

questions.explanation: Oregon law has strict mandatory penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: What should you NOT do if your friend has been drinking alcohol?

options.text: Arrange for a safe ride home for your friend.
Keep your friend busy with other activities.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: There are several ways to prevent someone from riding while impaired. Arrange another ride home, involve them in other activities, keep them from leaving before they are sober, and ask other friends to help intervene.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They involve riders with less than six months of experience.
They are caused by faulty ignition systems.
They occur because passengers distract the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with less than six months of experience.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a motorcycle that is new to you. Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders who have less than six months of experience on that bike.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride over an obstacle?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay on your seat and lift your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down. Approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle straight. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: Which item should you NOT check during a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride. Do a complete pre-ride inspection every time.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?

options.text: Prevent brakes from working on dry roads.
Alert you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.explanation: ABS prevents skidding and wheel lock-up during hard braking. It works when you apply maximum pressure to both brake controls. Sensors detect if a wheel is about to lock. The system then releases and reapplies brake pressure to keep maximum stopping power.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Check your mirrors and do a head check to look for traffic around you before changing lanes.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during the day, what should you do to reduce crash risk?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.

questions.explanation: Make yourself as visible as possible to reduce crash risk. Wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: Can common drugs like cold tablets affect your ability to ride safely?

options.text: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
Usually they won't affect your ability to ride safely.
No, they pose no risk to your riding ability.
No, they are always safe because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Learn about the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve:
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience. Most crashes happen during the day at low speeds.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Use the brake of the tire that is flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the good tire (if you know which one it is).

questions.question: How many drinks per hour does the body typically eliminate?
questions.explanation: The body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. The time it takes varies, so do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The rear brake is controlled by a pedal near the right footrest.

questions.question: A good lane position helps with all of these except:
questions.explanation: Your lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: When riding in fog, what lights should you use?

options.text: Alternate between low and high beams.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams near other vehicles.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you are slowing down where other drivers won't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are slowing down where other drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are hard to see. Flash your brake light before slowing down in places where other drivers might not expect it, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow cars, you should:

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly.
Weave between the cars to pass quickly.

questions.explanation: Riding between parked or slow cars is dangerous. Doors may open or cars may pull into traffic suddenly. If danger appears, you won't have room to escape safely. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers won't expect you there.
